channel.title: DISN Wildlife Research Project
channel.description: Recent content on DISN Wildlife Research Project

item.title: Tandon Research Excellence Expo (HILTS)
item.description: Juliana Barbosa, Eduarda Ramos, Gohar Petrossian, and Juliana Freire presented their research at the prestigious Tandon Research Excellence Expo, showcasing the innovative HILTS project and its impact on wildlife conservation efforts.

item.title: Juliana Freire
item.description: Juliana is a Tandon Institute Professor, Professor of Computer Science and Data Science at New York University, and co-director of the NYU Visualization, Imaging and Data Analysis (VIDA) Center.

item.title: Prevalence of endangered shark trophies in automated detection of the online wildlife trade
item.description: This paper examines the prevalence of endangered shark trophies in automated detection systems for online wildlife trade monitoring.

item.title: FBI New York Transnational Organized Crime Conference
item.description: Gohar Petrossian presented groundbreaking research on transnational wildlife crime at the 2025 FBI New York Transnational Organized Crime Eastern Hemisphere (TOC-E) Academic Conference, contributing to international law enforcement strategies.

item.title: Descriptive Analysis of Online Wildlife Products Using Vision Language Models
item.description: This paper presents a descriptive analysis of online wildlife products using vision language models for automated detection and classification.

item.title: Jennifer Jacquet
item.description: Jennifer Jacquet is a Professor of Environmental Science and Policy at the Rosenstiel School of Marine, Atmospheric, and Earth Science at the University of Miami, and affiliated faculty with the Abess Center for Ecosystem Science and Policy. She is also Associate Research Director of the Climate Social Science Network (CSSN) at Brown University.

item.title: Wildlife and Environmental Crime Summit
item.description: Gohar Petrossian served as a distinguished panelist and discussant at the Wildlife and Environmental Crime Summit hosted by Homeland Security Investigations, sharing expertise on combating environmental crimes and wildlife trafficking.

item.title: A Cost-Effective LLM-based Approach to Identify Wildlife Trafficking in Online Marketplaces
item.description: This paper introduces a cost-effective LLM-based approach to identify wildlife trafficking in online marketplaces, significantly reducing labeling costs while maintaining high accuracy.

item.title: Gohar Petrossian
item.description: Dr. Gohar Petrossian is Associate Professor in the Department of Criminal Justice, Director of the International Crime and Justice Master’s Program at John Jay College of Criminal Justice, and Deputy Executive Officer of the CUNY Graduate Center Criminal Justice Doctoral Program.

item.title: American Society of Criminology Conference
item.description: Ulhas Gondhali presented a comprehensive poster at the American Society of Criminology conference, showcasing innovative research methodologies in wildlife crime prevention and detection.

item.title: A Flexible and Scalable Approach for Collecting Wildlife Advertisements on the Web
item.description: This paper presents a flexible and scalable approach for collecting wildlife advertisements on the web, enabling large-scale data collection for wildlife trafficking research.

item.title: Sunandan Chakraborty
item.description: Sunandan Chakraborty focuses on data science for social good. Building computational models that leverage vast data sets, he applies them to a broad spectrum of problems in social and environmental science, agriculture, health, and other fields.

item.title: NSF DISN Conference 2023
item.description: Gohar Petrossian and Sunandan Chakraborty attended and presented at the prestigious NSF DISN Conference, demonstrating our interdisciplinary approach to discovering, analyzing, and disrupting wildlife trafficking networks.

item.title: HILTS: Human-LLM Collaboration for Effective Data Labeling
item.description: HILTS introduces a novel approach for human-LLM collaboration in data labeling tasks, improving efficiency and accuracy in wildlife trafficking detection.

item.title: Juliana Barbosa
item.description: Juliana is a Research Scientist at New York University - Visualization Imaging and Data Analysis Center.

item.title: InfoWild Workshop at HIS Conference 2023
item.description: Juliana Barbosa presented innovative research at the 1st CIKM International Workshop on Knowledge Extraction and Management for Wildlife Conservation, showcasing our flexible and scalable approach for collecting wildlife advertisements on the web.

item.title: Kinshuk Sharma
item.description: Kinshuk Sharma is a PhD candidate in Data Science at Indiana University Indianapolis. His research develops multimodal AI frameworks that combine computer vision and natural language processing to address real-world challenges in wildlife conservation.

item.title: Spencer Roberts
item.description: Spencer is a PhD Candidate at the University of Miami.

item.title: Joshua Lang
item.description: Joshua A. Lang is a doctoral student in the Criminal Justice program at John Jay College of Criminal Justice and CUNY Graduate Center. His research interests include wildlife crime, juvenile delinquency, and mental health within the criminal justice system.

item.title: Eduarda Ramos
item.description: Eduarda is a Computer Science PhD student at New York University - Visualization Imaging and Data Analysis Center.

item.title: Ulhas Gondhali
item.description: Ulhas Gondhali is a Ph.D. candidate at John Jay College of Criminal Justice, City University of New York. His research examines the intersections of illegal wildlife trade, illegal, unreported, and unregulated (IUU) fishing, maritime security, and transnational organized crime.

item.title: Julia von Ferber
item.description: Julia von Ferber, Ph.D. is an Assistant Professor for the Department of Security, Fire and Emergency Management (SFEM) at John Jay College of Criminal Justice, CUNY. Her research focuses on applying Crime Prevention Through Environmental Design (CPTED) to measure crime in privately owned public spaces and cybercrime.
